title: Mike Kelley: Ghost and Spirit

description.main: The Tate exhibition book for the first major UK exhibition of Mike Kelley (1954–2012), shown at Tate Modern from 3 October 2024 to 9 March 2025.
description.extended:
The catalogue of the first major UK exhibition of Mike Kelley (1954–2012), shown at Tate Modern from 3 October 2024 to 9 March 2025.

Catherine Wood, Tate Modern's Director of Programme, and Fiontán Moran edited the 304-page book, which has 200 illustrations and texts by contributors including Mark Beasley, Jack Halberstam, Mark Leckey and John Welchman. It follows Kelley's career from the late 1970s to 2012 through drawing, collage, performance, found objects and video, and covers the plush-toy and textile sculptures and installations such as Day Is Done. Tate Modern organised the exhibition with the Bourse de Commerce in Paris, K21 in Düsseldorf and the Moderna Museet in Stockholm.

Kelley took on different personas and media, and his work questioned assumptions about identity, class and institutional authority. He drew on popular and underground culture, literature and philosophy. Tate presents this as the first retrospective since his death, and the book as a case for his influence on art since the 1970s.
